repo_notes.content: SuperGrep is retrieval subagents for Claude Sonnet, built on the code-context CLI (bins `code-context` and `cx`) and MCP server: four tools over an index kept in two places. Three run locally over an index that lives in plain files under `.infino/`: find (every line containing an exact string, complete and unranked, like grep -n), search (BM25 keyword matching fused with vector similarity in one ranked pass), and sql (read-only SELECT/WITH over the index, with the ranked search functions usable as table-valued relations so search composes with GROUP BY). One runs in the cloud, over the same index's platform copy, when a platform database is configured with --db: ask (a question that spans the repository, handed to a small language model that queries the index itself, returned as the rows it found rather than as prose; several asks run at once). Drop the local half into Claude Code with `claude mcp add code-context -- npx -y @infino-ai/code-context mcp`, or install the CLI with `npm install -g @infino-ai/code-context` then `cx index` in a repo. Document it as subagents a coding agent delegates retrieval to instead of crawling files into its own context window: lead with the MCP setup, all four tools, and how the index stays fresh on its own (first query builds it, every query re-syncs it; there is no reindex tool).

Common misconceptions to avoid when documenting SuperGrep, with the corrected statements: (1) The published npm package needs NO account, API key, or database server - it runs locally, embedding uses a small local model downloaded once, and code never leaves the machine. That is the local half only. With a platform database configured (--db), ask runs in the cloud against a platform copy of the index: a bearer key authenticates the connection, and the platform's own model embeds that copy by default. Say which half a claim is about. (2) It is NOT semantic/vector search only. Local search is hybrid: BM25 and vector rankings fuse in one pass, and until vectors finish backfilling it degrades to keyword-only rather than failing. (3) The local index is NOT a proprietary database tier. It is plain files in `.infino/` that you can copy, cache in CI, or gitignore; the platform copy is a separate, server-side thing. (4) It is NOT a structural code-intelligence tool. It does ranked content retrieval and content-relevance aggregation, not call-graph tracing, dead-code detection, or type resolution; graph/LSP tools are complementary and stack alongside it. (5) On a blind judge, quality is NOT at parity with a frontier model's own file tools or its own Explore subagents - it loses aggregation, comprehension and by-meaning in both comparisons, and holds only the exact lookups (pinpoint, known-file). State the win as cost and speed on the categories it wins, not as an all-around replacement.

How it works: files are chunked at definition boundaries with tree-sitter (WASM, no native compile) for common languages, with a fixed-window fallback for the rest; every chunk carries path, start_line, end_line, lang, and content. Chunks are indexed into one table named `chunks`, with a BM25 full-text index and an IVF vector index. The local copy lives in `.infino/`, queried in-process through the infino engine's Node binding (no server); with --db the same chunks also load into a platform database, where ask runs against them. Readiness is staged: the keyword index commits in seconds so search is live immediately, while vectors backfill in the background and hybrid ranking unlocks automatically when they land. Sync is incremental: a per-file state map (size/mtime prefilter, then content hash) re-chunks and re-embeds only changed files, and every sync updates both copies when --db is set. The MCP surface is four tools: find (every line containing an exact string, cited path:line; the index's token match picks candidate chunks and each line is checked for the literal, so it is complete and unranked like grep -n), search (hybrid ranked retrieval), sql (read-only SELECT/WITH, with the ranked search functions bm25_search/hybrid_search usable as table-valued relations so search composes with GROUP BY aggregation), and ask (a question that spans the repository, run by a small language model against the platform copy and returned as the rows found rather than as prose; several asks run in parallel). Freshness is not a tool: the first query builds the index and every query re-syncs it; cx index --full rebuilds from a shell. The engine underneath is infino (https://github.com/infino-ai/infino), whose same index format also serves logs, docs, and agent memory.
